thread:
maria-support: Heads up — multiple customers (EU region) reporting intermittent 502/504s to the hosted API starting ~09:10 UTC. Affects both streaming and non-streaming. Sample trace id: tx-9f3a8b

deploy-bot: deploy finished: edge-proxy v2.3.7 rolled at 09:04 UTC (no rollback).

cheng-sre: on it. Can you paste a short repro (curl) and a few trace ids? Any customer request patterns (large embeddings, long streaming)?

maria-support: Repro steps (seen by eng support):
```
curl -sv https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"rw-large","input":"long prompt...","stream":true}'
```
Streaming requests are noisier but non-stream also sees 502s ~10% of calls during spike. Trace ids: tx-9f3a8b, tx-9f3a8d, tx-9f5b01.

liam-eng: pulled envoy logs for tx-9f3a8b:
```
[2026-03-17T09:12:01Z] "POST /v1/generate" 502 UPGRADE/STREAM 0 ms - upstream reset, reset_reason: connection failure, up_resp_code: 504
[2026-03-17T09:12:01Z] cluster_manager: cluster auth-service upstream reset, pending_streams=12
```
Looks like upstream auth/billing returning slowly and we get connection failures. Also saw a few GOAWAYs on h2 to auth-service.

sophia-observability: APM shows a p95 spike for oauth-token endpoint to ~2.8s starting 09:08 UTC. Downstream 5xx rate correlates with that window. Auth service error budget was hit briefly during a billing job at 09:05 that caused DB spikes.

maria-support: Customer said they rotated keys at 09:00 — could be causing auth-cache churn.

cheng-sre: hypothesis: h2 connection pool between edge and auth/billing is getting exhausted because tokens are invalidated and many upstream auth calls are reissued simultaneously. h2 keepalive/idle timeout + low pool size leads to queued streams -> envoy returns 502/504.

liam-eng: envoy shows max connection_retries exhausted and pending streams queuing per-worker. Snippet from envoy admin (conn/pool metrics):
```
edge.upstream.auth.active_connections: 48
edge.upstream.auth.pending_requests: 240
edge.upstream.auth.max_connections: 50
```
We hit pending queue saturation.

cheng-sre: mitigation options (short term):
- reduce http2_idle_timeout to free unused connections faster (default 300s -> 60s)
- bump max upstream connections for auth/billing by +30%
- add 1 retry for 502/504 with small backoff on edge proxy for idempotent calls
- route 10% of traffic to fallback model variant (stateless cached path) for heavy customers

kevin-platsec: increasing pool size could overload auth. Need to coordinate with auth team and limit per-customer concurrency. Also consider short-term 429 -> queueing vs failing.

liam-eng: I'll push a conservative config change to edge in canary: reduce http2_idle_timeout -> 60s and increase upstream_max_connections to 65 for auth/billing clusters in CANARY zone. Will monitor for auth DB pressure.

maria-support: please post the curl repro we can run internally with x-trace-id header so we can correlate.

sophia-observability: use this to force trace header:
```
curl -H "x-trace-id: test-502-0001" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" ...
```
I'll keep dashboards pinned and alert if 5xx > baseline for 10m.

liam-eng: applied canary at 09:34 UTC (edge-proxy cfg change: http2_idle_timeout=60s, upstream_max_connections=65). Canary is 3 nodes EU-west.

deploy-bot: config change deployed to edge-proxy CANARY cluster at 09:34:12 UTC (cfg-edge-2026-03-17-0900).

liam-eng: after canary, seen pending_requests drop ~85% on those nodes and 5xx rate in EU-west dropped from 8% -> 1.2% over 10m. No auth DB CPU spike observed so far.

cheng-sre: roll to 50% for EU at 09:42 UTC, full roll in 09:50 if stable. Also opened ticket AUTH-1739 to investigate key-rotation/thundering herd at auth side.

maria-support: customer-facing note: temporary config tweak deployed, asking impacted customers to retry. Will follow up with email and incident timeline.

kevin-platsec: please add a short-lived WAF rule to limit concurrency per API key while we investigate.

liam-eng: rolled to 100% EU at 09:52 UTC. Overall 502/504 volume back to baseline. Will keep monitoring for the next 3 hours and start a postmortem doc.

maria-support: thanks team — please drop postmortem link when ready. I'll update customers after final confirmation. :thumbsup:
